extracted.intended_audience: researchers (invited or prospective reviewers) for Royal Society journals; including early-career researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for performing peer review for Royal Society journals, covering reviewer qualifications, ethical expectations (bias/diversity/transparency), co‑reviewing, registration and recognition/rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base recommendations on scientific merits; avoid unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: We remind reviewers to be aware of any unconscious biases when assessing a paper. We are all susceptible to such biases and should take care that recommendations are based on the scientific merits of a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible biases to be aware of are country of origin, institution, name, gender, race and ethnicity to name a few.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications (minimum eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to be qualified at least PhD level (or equivalent) in a relevant subject, an active researcher and have published recently in one or more reputable peer reviewed journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have less experience, there is still the option to co-review with your supervisor or another colleague; approach them to express your interest so you can review with them and get recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept invitations when suitably qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are invited to review for one of our journals, and are suitably qualified to review the work, please try to say 'yes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing contributes to the quality and progression of science, reciprocates benefits when others review your papers, and helps your own research, professional development and profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co‑reviewing policy and recognition (consent requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A co-reviewer is defined as a researcher, often early in their career, who reviews a manuscript together with a more senior (invited) reviewer (see co-review policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is the opportunity for the senior reviewer to give recognition to the co-reviewer through the Reviewer Recognition Service and where we publish peer review reports by adding their name (provided consent has been given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and follow submission system / peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a journal reviewer, please register on ScholarOne. Once registered you will be considered as a reviewer for manuscripts that are within your research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are flagged within our system but we cannot guarantee that you will be selected as a reviewer for one of our journals. Read our peer review policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity by default; option to sign published reports (transparency choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five of our journals (Proceedings A, B, Biology Letters, Royal Society Open Science and Open Biology) offer transparency by publishing peer review information (reviewer reports, decision letter and response) under an open access licence (CC‑BY 4.0) alongside published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing in these journals is anonymous by default but reviewers have the option to sign their names to gain recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available supporting data and concise report forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting data for articles is easy to access; reviewer report forms are as concise as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Society offers email and telephone support to all reviewers and encourages reviewers to contact the Editorial Office of the journal if they require assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek training and guidance to improve reviewing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society encourages early‑career researchers to get involved in the peer review process and recommends training materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended resources include the Web of Science Academy, Nature Masterclasses, and the Society's peer review blog series (e.g., 'Tips for good practice in peer review' and 'What makes a good or a bad peer review?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors select reviewers based on relevant expertise and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Editors select reviewers based on relevant expertise from a wide and diverse pool of researchers from all over the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard: provide reviews within your area of expertise and ensure diversity of perspectives is supported by accepting or recommending other qualified reviewers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and rewards for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society journal reviewers receive a £200/$254/€233 discount on Article Processing Charges for publishing in our fully open access journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional recognition options: six journals publish annual citable articles listing reviewers who opted in; peer review certificates are available on request; the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service records and verifies peer review contributions (opt‑in via ScholarOne).
